title: Israeli Security Cabinet Convenes Emergency Meeting on Day 939 to Consider Resuming Full-Scale Gaza War as Disarmament Talks Fail; IDF Readying New Offensive
detail: On May 3, 2026 (Day 939 / Ceasefire Day 206), Israel's security cabinet convened an emergency session to formally weigh scenarios for resuming full-scale military operations in the Gaza Strip after Hamas's categorical refusal to enter Phase Two disarmament negotiations. The meeting marked the most explicit formal Israeli deliberation over ending the October 2025 ceasefire since its inception. Israeli officials stated that Hamas had failed to comply with any aspect of the disarmament framework advanced by the Board of Peace, and that the current ceasefire — which has seen 828+ Palestinian deaths and 2,400+ documented violations — was being exploited by Hamas to regroup rather than disarm. Defense ministers presented the cabinet with updated IDF operational plans for a new Gaza ground offensive designed to force Hamas demilitarization by military means. Al Jazeera reported that Israel was threatening 'Gaza war resumption to force disarmament as truce frays.' The Times of Israel reported that the IDF was 'readying a new Gaza offensive to disarm Hamas by force,' with the military having completed updated operational planning. The security cabinet did not issue a final decision at the May 3 session, but Israeli officials said 'all options are on the table.' The United States was briefed on Israel's deliberations; American officials urged continued diplomatic efforts before resuming military operations. Hamas responded that any resumption of war would be met with full resistance. The emergency session occurred 936 days after the October 7, 2023 attacks that initiated Operation Al-Aqsa Flood and Israel's subsequent Operation Swords of Iron.

media.caption: Israel's security cabinet considers resuming full-scale Gaza war as Hamas refuses disarmament; IDF readying new offensive — May 3, 2026

title: External IDF Panel Finds Most Internal October 7 Probes 'Inadequate'; Key Findings Omitted from Public Reports — Bereaved Families Demand Independent Commission
detail: On May 3, 2026 (Day 939), an external panel appointed by the IDF Chief of Staff released its assessment of the army's internal October 7 investigative probes — concluding that most were inadequate, with key findings omitted from public versions of the reports. The panel found that mid-level officers had reported 'a culture of complacency' in Southern Command that contributed to the October 7 catastrophe, but these findings were not reflected in public summary documents. The assessment came after the April 27 release of the IDF's final Holit probe (covering the Kibbutz Holit massacre, where ~60 Hamas Nukhba terrorists attacked the community, killing 13 civilians and 3 soldiers, with the community left without IDF reinforcement for 6 hours and 53 minutes). The Nir Oz probe released in February 2026 had similarly found that no military forces arrived until 1 p.m. — hours after Hamas fighters had left — and that a squadron en route was diverted mid-journey with no replacement sent. Former IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Herzi Halevi called the Nir Oz findings 'the failure within the failure of October 7.' Bereaved families described the external panel's findings as confirming their longstanding position that internal IDF probes were incapable of producing genuine accountability — only an independent state commission with subpoena power and authority to make personal findings of responsibility could provide real answers. The families' legal representatives stated they would present the external panel's findings to the Supreme Court before the July 1 deadline as evidence that self-investigation has failed.

media.caption: External IDF panel finds most internal October 7 probes inadequate; key findings omitted from public reports — May 2026
